items.name: Loss Analysis
items.summary: Governs the analytical framework the Actuarial department uses to understand how losses emerge, trend, and concentrate across the book, ensuring pricing, reserving, and portfolio decisions rest on a consistent, well-evidenced view of loss experience.

subs.title: Loss Development
subs.description: Loss development patterns must be measured and maintained for each line of business using paid and incurred triangles, with selected patterns reviewed at each analysis cycle. Material shifts in claim settlement or case reserving practice that distort development must be identified and adjusted for before patterns feed pricing or reserving work.

subs.title: Trend Analysis
subs.description: Frequency and severity trends are quantified separately where data permits, drawing on internal experience, industry sources, and economic indicators such as medical and social inflation. Selected trend rates carry documented rationale and are revisited whenever observed experience diverges from prior selections.

subs.title: Loss Ratio Benchmarking
subs.description: Loss ratios by line, segment, and program are compared against internal targets, plan assumptions, and available industry benchmarks on a regular cadence. Persistent deviations trigger root-cause analysis and a documented recommendation to pricing or underwriting leadership.

subs.title: Territory and Class Analysis
subs.description: Loss experience is segmented by territory and class of business to surface pockets of adverse or favorable performance hidden in aggregate results. Findings inform rate relativities, underwriting appetite, and growth strategy, with credibility procedures applied to thin segments.

items.name: CAT Model Selection
items.summary: Establishes the controls under which catastrophe models are chosen and deployed, so that the carrier's view of catastrophe risk is built on vetted, consistently applied modeling tools rather than ad hoc choices.

subs.title: Approved Vendor Models
subs.description: Only catastrophe models from vendors formally approved through the department's evaluation process may be used for pricing, accumulation, or capital purposes. The approved list specifies the perils, regions, and use cases each model is sanctioned for, and any use outside that scope requires documented exception approval.

subs.title: Version Control
subs.description: The model version in production use is recorded for every analysis, and migrations to new vendor releases follow a controlled adoption process that quantifies the change in modeled losses before cutover. Results produced on superseded versions remain traceable to the version that generated them.

subs.title: Model Blending Approach Documented
subs.description: Where multiple vendor models are blended to form the carrier's own view of risk, the blending weights, the rationale behind them, and any adjustments for non-modeled perils must be documented and approved. The blend is revisited when vendor releases or validation findings materially change relative model credibility.

items.name: CAT Model Validation
items.summary: Defines the ongoing testing regime that confirms catastrophe model output remains credible for the carrier's portfolio, protecting pricing, reinsurance purchase, and capital decisions from undetected model weakness.

subs.title: Annual Model Comparison
subs.description: Each year the department compares output across the approved vendor models, and against prior-year results on a constant portfolio, to isolate the drivers of change. Material divergences between models or between versions are explained and reflected in the documented blending decision.

subs.title: Backtesting Against Historical Events
subs.description: Modeled losses are reconciled against the carrier's actual experience from historical catastrophe events, including hurricanes, severe convective storms, and other relevant perils. Systematic over- or under-prediction is quantified and feeds adjustments to the carrier's own view of risk.

subs.title: Sensitivity Analysis
subs.description: Model results are stress-tested for sensitivity to key inputs such as exposure data quality, secondary modifiers, demand surge, and event frequency assumptions. The analysis identifies which assumptions most influence the loss estimates so reviewers understand the uncertainty surrounding reported PMLs.

items.name: Exposure Management
items.summary: Sets the requirements for monitoring and controlling catastrophe exposure accumulation across the portfolio, ensuring the carrier always knows where its concentrations sit and that they stay within approved tolerances.

subs.title: Aggregate Tracking
subs.description: Total insured values and modeled exposures are tracked continuously by peril, geography, and line of business as new and renewal business binds. The aggregation data must reconcile to policy administration systems and be refreshed frequently enough to support real-time underwriting referrals.

subs.title: Concentration Limits
subs.description: Board-approved concentration limits are maintained for each peril region, and exposure positions are measured against them on a defined cadence. Breaches or near-breaches trigger escalation to the chief actuary and chief underwriting officer with a documented remediation path.

subs.title: PML Analysis
subs.description: Probable maximum loss estimates are produced at the return periods relevant to reinsurance structuring, rating agency dialogue, and capital planning. Each PML run records the model version, portfolio snapshot date, and treatment of reinsurance so figures can be reproduced and compared over time.

subs.title: Zonal Reporting
subs.description: Exposure is reported by defined catastrophe zones, including coastal tiers, earthquake zones, and wildfire-prone territories, in a format consumable by underwriting, reinsurance, and executive audiences. Zonal reports highlight period-over-period movement and flag zones approaching their limits.

items.name: Capital Model Governance
items.summary: Prescribes the governance discipline surrounding the carrier's capital model so that the figures driving capital allocation, reinsurance strategy, and regulatory dialogue come from a controlled, independently challenged tool.

subs.title: Model Documentation
subs.description: The capital model's methodology, assumptions, data inputs, and known limitations are documented to a standard that allows a qualified actuary unfamiliar with the model to understand and rerun it. Documentation is kept current with each material model change.

subs.title: Change Control
subs.description: All modifications to the capital model follow a formal change process with documented justification, testing of the impact on results, and sign-off by the model owner before deployment. Emergency changes are permitted only with retrospective review and ratification.

subs.title: Independent Validation
subs.description: The model is validated on a defined cycle by reviewers independent of its development and operation, covering conceptual soundness, implementation accuracy, and outcome analysis. Validation findings are tracked to remediation and reported to the model governance committee.

subs.title: Version Control
subs.description: Every production run of the capital model is tied to a specific, archived model version, with code, parameters, and input data preserved. Superseded versions remain retrievable so historical capital figures can be reproduced for auditors and regulators.

items.name: Capital Requirements
items.summary: Governs how the carrier determines the capital it must hold, linking regulatory minimums, internal risk appetite, and adverse-scenario resilience into a single coherent capital adequacy view for management and the board.

subs.title: Regulatory Capital Calculations
subs.description: Risk-based capital and any other applicable regulatory capital measures are calculated accurately and on the prescribed schedule for each legal entity. Calculations reconcile to filed statutory statements, and movements between periods are explained to management before filing.

subs.title: Internal Capital Targets
subs.description: Internal capital targets are set above regulatory minimums to reflect rating agency expectations, risk appetite, and growth plans, and are approved by the board. Actual capital positions are monitored against these targets with defined escalation thresholds well before regulatory action levels.

subs.title: Stress Testing
subs.description: Capital adequacy is tested under a documented suite of adverse scenarios, including severe catastrophe seasons, reserve deterioration, investment shocks, and combined events. Stress results inform contingency capital plans and are presented to the risk committee at least annually.

items.name: Risk Aggregation
items.summary: Defines how individual risk measurements are combined into an enterprise-level view of required capital, ensuring dependency assumptions and diversification effects are explicit, justified, and transparent to decision-makers.

subs.title: Correlation Assumptions
subs.description: Dependencies between risk types, lines of business, and entities are captured through documented correlation or copula assumptions with stated rationale and supporting evidence. Assumptions receive heightened scrutiny in the tail, where historical correlations tend to strengthen, and are reviewed on a regular cycle.

subs.title: Diversification Benefit
subs.description: The capital reduction attributed to diversification across the multi-line book is quantified, attributed back to its sources, and disclosed alongside undiversified figures. The benefit is tested for stability under stressed dependency assumptions before being relied upon in capital decisions.

subs.title: Risk Distribution by Source
subs.description: Aggregate required capital is decomposed by risk source, including underwriting, reserve, catastrophe, market, credit, and operational risk, so management can see what drives the capital position. The attribution supports capital allocation to business units and pricing for the cost of capital.

items.name: Experience Monitoring
items.summary: Establishes the discipline of continuously comparing emerging experience to pricing expectations, so the carrier detects pricing inadequacy or redundancy early and corrects course before results deteriorate.

subs.title: Actual Versus Expected Analysis
subs.description: Emerging loss, frequency, and severity experience is compared against the assumptions embedded in current rates on a regular cadence by line and segment. Deviations are decomposed into their drivers, distinguishing random volatility from genuine assumption misses.

subs.title: Pricing Feedback Loop
subs.description: Monitoring findings flow back into the next pricing review through a defined process connecting the monitoring team, pricing actuaries, and underwriting. The loop ensures assumption updates are grounded in observed experience rather than carried forward by inertia.

subs.title: Adjustment Recommendations
subs.description: When monitored experience diverges materially from expectations, the department issues documented recommendations covering rate level, segmentation, or underwriting action, with quantified support. Recommendations are tracked through to disposition so accepted and rejected actions are both on record.

items.name: Pricing Methodology
items.summary: Governs the technical foundation of how rates are built across the carrier's lines of business, ensuring every rate level traces to a documented, actuarially sound method rather than judgment applied inconsistently.

subs.title: Documented Pricing Approach by Line of Business
subs.description: Each line of business maintains a written pricing methodology covering data sources, ratemaking technique, expense and profit provisions, and treatment of reinsurance costs. The documentation is owned by a named actuary and updated whenever the approach materially changes.

subs.title: Actuarial Indication Basis
subs.description: Rate indications are produced on a consistent, documented basis specifying the experience period, premium on-level adjustments, loss trending, and credibility procedures. Departures of filed or implemented rates from the actuarial indication are recorded with business rationale.

subs.title: Loss Development Factors
subs.description: Development factors used in ratemaking are derived from current triangles using documented selection criteria, with consistency checks against the factors used in reserving. Selections are refreshed each pricing cycle and material changes from prior selections are explained.

items.name: Rate Adequacy Review
items.summary: Requires a periodic, evidence-based assessment of whether current rate levels are sufficient to cover expected losses, expenses, and target profit, giving leadership early warning of inadequacy across the portfolio.

subs.title: Annual Rate Adequacy Analysis
subs.description: Every rated line of business undergoes a formal rate adequacy study at least annually, comparing current rate levels to indicated levels. Lines found inadequate carry a documented action plan, whether a filing, underwriting tightening, or accepted deviation with rationale.

subs.title: Loss Ratio Projections
subs.description: Prospective loss ratios are projected for the period the rates will be in effect, reflecting trended losses, on-level premium, and expected mix shifts. Projections state their key assumptions and are reconciled retrospectively against actual results to sharpen future analyses.

subs.title: Trend Assumptions Documented
subs.description: The frequency, severity, and premium trend assumptions underlying each adequacy review are recorded with their data sources and selection rationale. Reviewers can therefore trace any indicated rate need back to the specific trend selections that produced it.

items.name: Rate Filing Support
items.summary: Defines the actuarial work product and engagement model that supports rate filings with state regulators, ensuring submissions are technically defensible and regulator questions are answered accurately and promptly.

subs.title: Actuarial Memorandum
subs.description: Each rate filing includes an actuarial memorandum prepared in accordance with applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice, describing the data, methods, assumptions, and judgments behind the requested rate change. The memorandum is signed by a qualified actuary who takes responsibility for the work.

subs.title: Supporting Exhibits
subs.description: Filings are accompanied by exhibits presenting the experience data, development, trend, on-level calculations, and indicated versus selected rates in the format each state expects. Exhibits must tie to the underlying analysis workpapers without manual reconciliation gaps.

subs.title: Regulatory Response Coordination
subs.description: Objections and interrogatories from state insurance departments are routed through a defined process pairing the filing actuary with compliance, with response deadlines tracked and met. Responses are reviewed for technical accuracy and consistency with positions taken in other jurisdictions.

items.name: Filing Support
items.summary: Governs the actuarial contribution to product-related rate and form filings, ensuring new and revised products reach regulators with sound actuarial backing and that objections are resolved without stalling launches.

subs.title: Rate and Form Filing Support
subs.description: Actuarial staff supply the rate exhibits, rating algorithm specifications, and actuarial justification needed for rate and form filings across the product portfolio. Support includes verifying that filed rating rules can actually be implemented as described in policy administration systems.

subs.title: Actuarial Certification
subs.description: Where states require certification that filed rates are not excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory, a qualified actuary performs the supporting review and signs the certification. The certifying actuary's workpapers are retained as evidence of the basis for the opinion.

subs.title: Objection Response
subs.description: Actuarial objections raised against product filings are answered with technically complete responses within regulator deadlines, coordinated with product and compliance teams. Recurring objection themes are catalogued and fed back into filing preparation to reduce future cycle time.

items.name: Product Pricing Review
items.summary: Requires structured actuarial scrutiny before new products go to market, confirming that pricing is competitively positioned and expected to meet the carrier's profitability hurdles across its P&C, life, and group benefits lines.

subs.title: New Product Actuarial Sign-Off
subs.description: No new product launches without documented sign-off from the responsible pricing actuary covering the rating plan, assumptions, and expected profitability. The sign-off identifies key uncertainties and the monitoring plan that will validate assumptions post-launch.

subs.title: Competitive Analysis
subs.description: Proposed rates are benchmarked against competitor filings and market intelligence to assess positioning by segment and the risk of adverse selection. The analysis distinguishes deliberate competitive stances from unintended pricing gaps before launch approval.

subs.title: Profit Testing
subs.description: New products are profit-tested against the carrier's return targets using projected loss ratios, expenses, persistency, and cost of capital, with sensitivity runs on the most uncertain assumptions. Products failing the hurdle require redesign or explicit executive acceptance of the shortfall.

items.name: Reinsurance Credit
items.summary: Governs the actuarial valuation and ongoing assessment of amounts recoverable from reinsurers, ensuring ceded balances on the balance sheet are accurate, collectible, and supportable when treaties are unwound.

subs.title: Ceded Reserve Calculation
subs.description: Ceded loss and loss adjustment expense reserves are calculated by treaty in accordance with contract terms, including attachment points, limits, and reinstatement provisions. Ceded figures reconcile to gross and net reserve analyses so the three views remain internally consistent.

subs.title: Collectability Analysis
subs.description: Recoverables are assessed for collectability based on reinsurer financial strength, ratings, disputes, and aging of paid balances, with provisions for uncollectible amounts established where warranted. Concentrations with individual reinsurers are monitored against counterparty limits.

subs.title: Commutation Support
subs.description: When treaty commutations are contemplated, the department values the ceded liabilities being extinguished, including discounting and risk margins, to support negotiation of the commutation price. The analysis quantifies the balance sheet and income impact of accepting versus declining the commutation.

items.name: Reinsurance Pricing
items.summary: Defines the actuarial analysis behind the carrier's reinsurance purchasing decisions, ensuring ceded programs are priced, structured, and evaluated on a rigorous economic basis rather than market habit.

subs.title: Ceded Pricing Analysis
subs.description: Quoted reinsurance terms are evaluated against the department's own loss cost estimates for the ceded layers, derived from experience and exposure rating. The analysis expresses each quote as a rate-on-line and expected economic margin so negotiators understand what they are paying for risk transfer.

subs.title: Treaty Optimization
subs.description: Alternative program structures, including retention levels, layer boundaries, and quota share versus excess arrangements, are modeled for their effect on net volatility, capital relief, and expected cost. Recommendations to the reinsurance buying team balance earnings protection against ceded margin.

subs.title: Retrocession Analysis Support
subs.description: Where the carrier assumes business or participates in structures with retrocession features, the department analyzes the retro protections available and their effect on net positions. Support covers pricing the retro layers and assessing counterparty and basis risk in the proposed cover.

items.name: Actuarial Reporting
items.summary: Establishes the suite of recurring actuarial communications to governance bodies, management, and regulators, ensuring each audience receives accurate, decision-ready insight on reserves, pricing, and risk on the required cadence.

subs.title: Board Reporting
subs.description: The chief actuary delivers periodic reporting to the board and its committees covering reserve adequacy, pricing trends, catastrophe exposure, and emerging risks, in language suited to a governance audience. Material adverse developments are escalated between scheduled cycles rather than held for the next meeting.

subs.title: Management Dashboards
subs.description: Operational dashboards present key actuarial indicators, including loss ratio trends, reserve movements, and rate change achievement, refreshed on a defined schedule. Metrics carry consistent definitions across business units so management comparisons are like-for-like.

subs.title: Regulatory Statements
subs.description: Actuarial inputs to statutory filings, including Schedule P support and the Statement of Actuarial Opinion, are produced accurately and on the regulatory calendar. Figures in regulatory statements reconcile to internal analyses, with differences in basis documented.

subs.title: ORSA Support
subs.description: The department supplies the quantitative content for the Own Risk and Solvency Assessment, including capital projections, stress scenarios, and risk quantification across the planning horizon. Contributions align with the capital model and risk appetite framework so the ORSA tells one consistent story.

items.name: IBNR Development
items.summary: Governs how incurred-but-not-reported reserves are estimated, ensuring the largest judgment-driven component of the carrier's liabilities is built at appropriate granularity and presented with honest uncertainty bounds.

subs.title: IBNR Factors by Line of Business and Accident Year
subs.description: IBNR is estimated at the level of line of business and accident year, using factors derived from the selected development patterns and expected loss methods appropriate to each cohort's maturity. Factor selections are documented and reconciled to the prior review so movements are explainable.

subs.title: Sensitivity Analysis
subs.description: The IBNR estimate is tested for sensitivity to the key assumptions, including tail factors, trend, and expected loss ratios, quantifying how plausible alternative selections would move the booked reserve. Results inform management's understanding of where the estimate is most fragile.

subs.title: Range of Estimates
subs.description: A reasonable range around the central IBNR estimate is produced and communicated, with the booked position located explicitly within that range. Movement of the booked reserve relative to the range over time is monitored as an indicator of reserving strength or weakening.

items.name: Reserve Documentation
items.summary: Sets the documentation standard for reserve analyses so that conclusions, the reasoning behind them, and changes from prior reviews are transparent to management, auditors, and regulators.

subs.title: Actuarial Report with Key Assumptions
subs.description: Each reserve review produces a formal actuarial report meeting ASOP 41 communication standards, setting out data, methods, key assumptions, and the basis for selections. The report is sufficient for another qualified actuary to assess the reasonableness of the conclusions.

subs.title: Management Summary
subs.description: A concise summary translates the technical findings into the booked reserve recommendation, the drivers of change, and the principal uncertainties, written for senior management and the audit committee. The summary states clearly where the recommendation sits relative to the actuarial central estimate.

subs.title: Variance Explanation
subs.description: Differences between the current estimate and the prior review, and between actual emergence and what was expected, are quantified and attributed to their causes. Persistent one-directional variances are flagged as potential evidence of assumption bias requiring correction.

items.name: Reserve Methodology
items.summary: Prescribes the technical methods underpinning reserve estimation across the carrier's lines, ensuring methods, data organization, and factor derivation are applied consistently and remain fit for each line's characteristics.

subs.title: Methods Documented by Line of Business
subs.description: The reserving methods applied to each line, such as chain ladder, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, and expected loss ratio approaches, are documented along with the criteria for weighting them by accident year maturity. Method changes require justification and quantification of their impact before adoption.

subs.title: Triangle Selection
subs.description: The choice of triangle basis for each analysis, including paid versus incurred, accident versus report year, and the level of segmentation, is documented with rationale tied to the line's claim characteristics. Segmentation is revisited when business mix or volume changes erode the homogeneity or credibility of existing groupings.

subs.title: Development Factor Derivation
subs.description: Age-to-age factors are derived using stated averaging conventions, with outlier treatment, tail factor methodology, and the rationale for final selections recorded. Selected factors are compared against prior selections and industry benchmarks to confirm reasonableness.

items.name: Reserve Review Process
items.summary: Defines the cadence and escalation of reserve oversight throughout the year, layering routine monitoring, periodic deep analysis, and independent year-end challenge so reserve adequacy is never assessed only once annually.

subs.title: Monthly Reserve Review
subs.description: Actual loss emergence is compared to expected each month at a summary level, with material deviations investigated and escalated to the chief actuary. The monthly process is designed to surface deterioration quickly rather than re-estimate the full reserve.

subs.title: Quarterly Deep Dive
subs.description: A full reserve study updating triangles, selections, and IBNR is performed each quarter, with results presented to management before the financial close. Each quarter rotates additional focus onto lines showing volatility or strategic significance.

subs.title: Year-End External Review
subs.description: The year-end reserve position is subject to independent review by an external actuarial firm or appointed actuary engagement, supporting the Statement of Actuarial Opinion. Differences between external and internal estimates are reconciled and reported to the audit committee.

items.name: Actuarial Standards of Practice
items.summary: Anchors all actuarial work to professional standards and qualified accountability, ensuring the department's analyses and opinions withstand professional, audit, and regulatory scrutiny.

subs.title: Compliance with Actuarial Standards of Practice
subs.description: All actuarial work products comply with the applicable ASOPs issued by the Actuarial Standards Board, including those governing data quality, assumptions, and communications. Deviations from a standard are permitted only where the ASOP itself allows and must be disclosed in the work product.

subs.title: Peer Review Process
subs.description: Significant analyses, including reserve studies, rate indications, and capital work, receive documented peer review by a qualified actuary not involved in the original work before release. Review comments and their resolution are retained with the workpapers.

subs.title: Actuarial Opinion Sign-Off
subs.description: Formal opinions, including the Statement of Actuarial Opinion on reserves, are signed only by appointed actuaries meeting the qualification standards of the American Academy of Actuaries. The signing actuary maintains the supporting actuarial opinion summary and workpapers required by regulators.

items.name: Data Quality
items.summary: Establishes the data integrity controls underlying all actuarial analysis, so that pricing, reserving, and capital conclusions rest on data whose accuracy, completeness, and limitations are known and disclosed.

subs.title: Data Validation
subs.description: Data received for actuarial use is checked for reasonableness, completeness, and internal consistency before analysis begins, consistent with ASOP 23. Anomalies such as negative payments, missing accident dates, or implausible values are investigated and their treatment documented.

subs.title: Reconciliation to Source Systems
subs.description: Actuarial data extracts are reconciled to the policy, claims, and general ledger systems they originate from, with premium and loss totals tied out each analysis cycle. Unreconciled differences beyond defined tolerances must be resolved or explained before the data is used.

subs.title: Known Data Limitations Documented
subs.description: Limitations in the available data, such as system conversions, coding changes, or thin volume in newer segments, are catalogued and disclosed in the work products that rely on the data. Analysts document how each limitation was addressed and its potential effect on the conclusions.
